title: Graph construction of the global Frobenius operator
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]
and the coefficient conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], and let $(K,\varphi)$ be a
strict Weil complex of
[def-trf-strict-weil-complex]. For $m\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$ let
$\Phi^m$ be the $m$-fold iterate of the
scheme Frobenius of
[def-trf-scheme-frobenius] and
$u_m:L\Phi^{m*}K\to K$ the
scheme-Frobenius map of
[def-trf-iterated-weil-map], and consider the
graph correspondence of [def-trf-graph-correspondence]
$c=(\operatorname{id}_X,\Phi^m)$ with $u_m$. Then its
global operator $T_c(u_m)$ of
[def-trf-global-operator], identified as in
[prop-trf-graph-operator], equals the $m$-th iterate of the
global geometric Frobenius:

$$
T_c(u_m)=F_{c,K}^{\,m}:
R\Gamma_c(X,K)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_c(X,K),
$$

where $F_{c,K}^{\,m}$ is the endomorphism of the
global geometric Frobenius
operator of [def-trf-frobenius-operators] with its finite-coefficient compact-support transport
of [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport]. The equality is natural in
$(K,\varphi)$ and compatible with the cocycle law in $m$.

Here the comparison $\kappa^{(m)}$ is the canonical one: using
$\Phi^m=g_\gamma^m\operatorname{Fr}_X^{(q^m)}$ from
[prop-trf-frobenius-factorization], it is the composite, with the canonical pullback-composition identification of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition],
$$
L\Phi^{m*}\simeq L(\operatorname{Fr}_X^{(q^m)})^*Lg_\gamma^{m*}
\xrightarrow{\ t_X^{(am)}\ }Lg_\gamma^{m*},
$$
where $t_X^{(am)}$ is the multiplicative absolute-Frobenius
trivialization of [lem-trf-absolute-frobenius-site]. In particular it
uses the canonical constant-coefficient identifications, with no
scalar rescaling.

More generally, let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ carry no Weil structure and
let $v:Lg_\gamma^{m*}K\to K$ be an arbitrary morphism, not necessarily
invertible. Then the graph correspondence $c=(\operatorname{id}_X,\Phi^m)$
with $\kappa^{(m)}$ of [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison]
and coefficient map $v\circ\kappa^{(m)}_K:L\Phi^{m*}K\to K$ has

$$
T_c\bigl(v\circ\kappa^{(m)}_K\bigr)
=R\Gamma_c(X,v)\circ g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}:
R\Gamma_c(X,K)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_c(X,K),
$$

where $g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}:R\Gamma_c(X,K)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_c(X,Lg_\gamma^{m*}K)$
is the compact-support base-change isomorphism along $g_\gamma^m$; the
displayed identity $T_c(u_m)=F_{c,K}^{\,m}$ is the case $v=\varphi^{[m]}$.

proof.text:
Write $P_m=L\Phi^{m*}$, $G_m=Lg_\gamma^{m*}$ and $H=R\Gamma_c(X,-)$. The scheme map $\Phi$ is the scalar-extended $q$-power Frobenius constructed in [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. Its finiteness is the assertion of [lem-trf-scheme-frobenius-finite-radicial], applied to the same finite-field datum and finite-type model $X_0$; this assertion requires neither reducedness nor separatedness of the model. Its iterates are proper without any new finiteness lemma: the identity is proper (its diagonal is an isomorphism, it is of finite type, and every base change is the identity). If $\Phi^r$ is proper, apply clause (c) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence] to the finite map $f=\Phi$ and the proper map $h=\Phi^r$; the composite is $\Phi^{r+1}$. Induction gives properness for every $r\geq0$. For any $w:P_mK\to K$, [prop-trf-graph-operator] therefore gives
$$T_{(\mathrm{id},\Phi^m)}(w)=H(w)\circ e_{m,K},$$
where $e_{m,K}:H(K)\to H(P_mK)$ is the pullback/direct-image unit followed by proper coincidence and compact-support composition, exactly as specified by [def-trf-global-operator].

source.place: Opening paragraph: properness and expansion of the graph operator

proof.text: Choose a compactification $j_0:X_0\hookrightarrow\bar X_0$ over $k_0$ by [prop-compactification-refinement] applied to $X_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$. Its base change is $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$: on underlying open subschemes it identifies $X$ with the inverse image of the open $X_0\subset\bar X_0$, since the fiber product of an open subscheme is exactly that inverse-image open. The base-changed compactification has proper structure map by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. A bounded constructible finite-coefficient complex has an etale-origin witness by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], so [lem-trf-compactification-cohomology] applies to $K$ and to its Galois pullbacks. Set $M=j_!K$ and write $C_K:H(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(\bar X,M)$. By [lem-trf-compactification-graph-operator], for every $w:P_mK\to K$, the operator of Step 1 is conjugate under $C_K$ to the proper graph operator with coefficient map $\bar w=j_!w\circ b_{\Phi,m}$, where $b_{\Phi,m}:L\bar\Phi^{m*}j_!\simeq j_!P_m$. The finite-Tor assertion $M\in D^b_{ctf}(\bar X,A)$ is supplied directly by [lem-trf-open-ctf].

source.place: Step 2: compute the specified compact-support maps in a compactification

proof.text:
Here is the normalization check on the proper scheme $\bar X$, rather than an inference from uniqueness of right adjoints alone. Put $\bar P_m=L\bar\Phi^{m*}$, $\bar G_m=Lg_{\gamma,\bar X}^{m*}$, and $\bar\kappa_m:\bar P_m\simeq\bar G_m$ from [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison]. The factorization in [prop-trf-frobenius-factorization] and the canonical absolute-Frobenius trivialization of [lem-trf-absolute-frobenius-site] construct the explicitly specified comparison in the statement. On a constant sheaf the relative-Frobenius identification of site objects acts by restriction on locally constant functions: restriction sends the constant function $1$ to $1$, and so do its inverse and every iterate. Consequently the component of this comparison on the constant coefficient sheaf preserves $1$. Write $d_P:\bar P_m A_{\bar X}\simeq A_{\bar X}$ and $d_G:\bar G_m A_{\bar X}\simeq A_{\bar X}$ for the canonical constant-sheaf identifications. Thus $d_G\bar\kappa_{m,A}=d_P$. For a sheaf $N$, a section is a map $s:A_{\bar X}\to N$. Its pullback section under either functor $Q=\bar P_m,\bar G_m$ is $Q(s)d_Q^{-1}$. Naturality now gives the actual equality
$$\bar\kappa_{m,N}\bar P_m(s)d_P^{-1}=\bar G_m(s)\bar\kappa_{m,A}d_P^{-1}=\bar G_m(s)d_G^{-1}.$$
This holds degreewise on complexes, not merely on cohomology groups. The finite-level clause of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] represents every scheme pullback by exact termwise inverse image with the canonical constant-ring identification. In particular both $\bar P_m$ and $\bar G_m$ here are represented on sheaves, and the specified relative-Frobenius comparison extends termwise. At finite constant coefficients [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback] identifies the pullback along the scheme automorphism $g_{\gamma,\bar X}^m$ with termwise inverse image. Its inverse is inverse image along $g_{\gamma,\bar X}^{-m}$, with the canonical composition identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. Hence $\bar G_m$ is an exact equivalence, as is $\bar P_m\simeq\bar G_m$. They carry injectives to injectives: for an injective $I$, the functor $\operatorname{Hom}(-,QI)=\operatorname{Hom}(Q^{-1}(-),I)$ is exact because $Q^{-1}$ is exact. They also preserve K-injective complexes: for acyclic $B^\bullet$, the complex $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(B^\bullet,QI^\bullet)$ identifies with $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(Q^{-1}B^\bullet,I^\bullet)$ and is acyclic. Using the K-injective construction of [def-weil-derived-direct-image], the displayed degreewise equation gives
$$R\Gamma(\bar X,\bar\kappa_{m,M})\circ\rho_{P,M}=\rho_{G,M}$$
in $D(A)$, where $\rho$ denotes ordinary cohomology pullback. The ordinary cohomology and point fiber are precisely those of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] and [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. The pullback/direct-image units induce these section maps by their definition; their derived compatibility is also the unit equation $G_2\alpha\circ\beta F_1\circ\eta_1=\eta_2$ of [lem-trf-adjoint-mate].

source.place: Step 1 and Step 2: comparison of units with the canonical section maps

proof.text:
We identify the compact-support transport with the map just computed, keeping the semilinear base map. The Galois map satisfies $\bar a\,g_{\gamma,\bar X}^m=g_s^m\bar a$, not $\bar a\,g_{\gamma,\bar X}^m=\bar a$; use the Frobenius square of [lem-weil-frobenius-square-cartesian], with the datum $q^m$. Concretely, base change the model $X_0$ to the degree-$m$ subfield $k_m\subset k$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]; its geometric fiber is still $X$, and its one-step geometric Frobenius is $g_\gamma^m$. Do the same for $\bar X_0$. The ordinary exchange and point transport in [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange] and [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] yield ordinary pullback $\rho_G$, as the following explicit adjunction calculation shows. Put $F=L\bar a^*$, $R=R\bar a_*$, $B=L(g_s^m)^*$, and $T=\bar G_m$. Write $\theta:FB\simeq TF$ for the canonical square comparison. The exchange $E:BR\to RT$ is
$$E_N=R(T\varepsilon_N)\circ R(\theta_{RN})\circ\eta_{BRN}.$$
A section $s:A_{\bar X}\to N$ corresponds to $z:A_s\to RN$ with $s=\varepsilon_N\circ F(z)$, using $FA_s=A_{\bar X}$. Point transport sends $z$ to $B(z)\circ d_B^{-1}$, where $d_B:BA_s\simeq A_s$ is the constant-coefficient identification: this is precisely restriction and insertion in the stated point-transport definition. The transpose of its image under $E_N$ is
$$\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon_{TN}\circ F(E_N)\circ FB(z)\circ F(d_B^{-1})
&=T(\varepsilon_N)\circ\theta_{RN}\circ FB(z)\circ F(d_B^{-1})\\
&=T(\varepsilon_N\circ F(z))\circ\theta_{A_s}\circ F(d_B^{-1})\\
&=T(s)\circ d_T^{-1}.
\end{aligned}$$
The first equality expands the displayed mate and cancels the adjunction triangle; the second is naturality of $\theta$; the last uses $\theta_{A_s}\circ F(d_B^{-1})=d_T^{-1}$, since the square pullback comparison identifies the same constant section $1$. Thus this is exactly the section map of Step 3, including its normalization. For the derived assertion choose a K-injective representative $I^\bullet$ of $M$. The finite-level exactness in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] allows the preceding calculation to be made degreewise with $F=\bar a^*$, $R=\bar a_*$, $B=(g_s^m)^*$ and $T=g_{\gamma,\bar X}^{m*}$ on sheaves. The complex $\bar a_*I^\bullet$ is K-injective because $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(B^\bullet,\bar a_*I^\bullet)=\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(\bar a^*B^\bullet,I^\bullet)$ is acyclic for every acyclic $B^\bullet$, using exactness of $\bar a^*$. The scheme-isomorphism inverse images $B,T$ preserve K-injectives by the exact-inverse argument of Step 3. Thus these complexes compute the displayed derived direct images and the specified derived mate, giving the equality in $D(A)$.

The open squares for both Frobenii are Cartesian by [lem-trf-frobenius-open-square]. Their canonical comparisons $b_{\Phi,m}$ and $b_{G,m}$ are provided by [lem-trf-open-square-exchange]. They satisfy
$$b_{G,m}\circ\bar\kappa_{m,j_!K}=j_!\kappa^{(m)}_K\circ b_{\Phi,m}.$$
Indeed, restrict to $X$: the comparisons are identities there and the two absolute-Frobenius trivializations restrict to the same one by [lem-trf-absolute-frobenius-site]. Both sides are maps between extensions by zero. The derived adjunction and invertible unit of [prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions] identify $\operatorname{Hom}(j_!B,j_!D)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(B,D)$, so their restrictions determine them. The compactification formula in item 2 of [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange], followed by point transport, consequently says
$$C_{G_mK}\circ\tau_{m,K}=R\Gamma(\bar X,b_{G,m,K})\circ\rho_{G,j_!K}\circ C_K,$$
where $\tau_{m,K}=g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}$ is the finite-coefficient transport of [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport]. Its being an isomorphism, also for the datum $q^m$, is [lem-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport-iso]. This uses the same chosen compactification throughout.

source.place: Step 2: identify the compact-support exchange, including its base-point transport

proof.text:
Let $v:G_mK\to K$ be arbitrary and put $w=v\kappa^{(m)}_K$. On the compactification, Step 2 gives $\bar w=j_!v\circ j_!\kappa^{(m)}_K\circ b_{\Phi,m}$. Substituting the open-comparison equation of Step 4 and the section-map equation of Step 3, the graph formula of [prop-trf-graph-operator] on the proper scheme $\bar X$ becomes
$$T_{\bar c}(\bar w)=R\Gamma(\bar X,j_!v)\circ R\Gamma(\bar X,b_{G,m})\circ\rho_G.$$
Here proper coincidence [prop-weil-proper-compact-coincidence] identifies the compact-support graph formula with ordinary cohomology, using the identity compactification; no semilinear Galois map is treated as a $k$-endomorphism in that formula. Step 4 identifies the right side, after conjugation by $C_K$, with $H(v)\tau_{m,K}$. Naturality of $C$ from [lem-trf-compactification-cohomology] and the graph intertwining of [lem-trf-compactification-graph-operator] therefore give
$$T_c(v\kappa^{(m)}_K)=H(v)\tau_{m,K}.$$
No Weil datum or inverse of $v$ has entered this argument, so this proves the full arbitrary-coefficient-map assertion.

source.place: Step 3: arbitrary coefficient maps, without invertibility

proof.text:
For a strict Weil complex take $v=\varphi^{[m]}$. The definition [def-trf-iterated-weil-map] gives $u_m=\varphi^{[m]}\kappa^{(m)}_K$. Step 5 and [lem-trf-frobenius-operator-compact-description] then give
$$T_c(u_m)=H(\varphi^{[m]})\tau_{m,K}=F_{c,K}^{\,m}.$$
For a morphism $a:(K,\varphi)\to(L,\psi)$ of [def-trf-strict-weil-complex], the defining morphism condition is $a\varphi=\psi G_1(a)$, giving the case $m=1$. If $a\varphi_K^{[r]}=\psi_L^{[r]}G_r(a)$, the defining iterates give, under the canonical pullback-composition identifications,
$$a\varphi_K^{[r+1]}=a\varphi G_1(\varphi_K^{[r]})=\psi G_1(a\varphi_K^{[r]})=\psi G_1(\psi_L^{[r]})G_{r+1}(a)=\psi_L^{[r+1]}G_{r+1}(a).$$
Thus the intertwining identity holds for every $m\geq1$. Naturality of $\kappa^{(m)}$ and of $\tau_m$ gives $H(a)H(\varphi_K^{[m]})\tau_{m,K}=H(\psi_L^{[m]})\tau_{m,L}H(a)$, which is the asserted naturality.

source.place: Step 2: specialization to the strict Weil map and naturality

proof.text:
Finally, the ordinary pullback of a section along a composite is the composite of its pullbacks: $(g^m)^*((g^n)^*s)=(g^{m+n})^*s$, with the canonical pullback-composition identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], whose statement specifies the termwise maps. This is an equality of the maps of complexes used in Step 3. The identity/pasting property of [lem-trf-open-square-exchange] and the compactification formula of [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange] therefore give
$$\tau_{m+n,K}=\tau_{m,G_nK}\circ\tau_{n,K}.$$
This also proves the requisite transitivity for these specific exchanges; it is not inferred from an unspecified coherence record. Write $\varphi_m=\varphi^{[m]}$. Using [lem-trf-iterated-weil-cocycle] and naturality of $\tau_m$ with respect to the map $\varphi_n:G_nK\to K$, we get
$$\begin{aligned}
H(\varphi_{m+n})\tau_{m+n,K}
&=H(\varphi_m)H(G_m\varphi_n)\tau_{m,G_nK}\tau_{n,K}\\
&=H(\varphi_m)\tau_{m,K}H(\varphi_n)\tau_{n,K}.
\end{aligned}$$
The compact-description lemma [lem-trf-frobenius-operator-compact-description] identifies these with $F_{c,K}^{m+n}$ and $F_{c,K}^mF_{c,K}^n$. Taking $m=1$ and inducting identifies them with powers of the one-step operator. For the transport itself, the degree-one datum gives $\tau_{1,K}=\tau_{c,K}$. Taking $m=1,n=r$ in the proved transport equation gives $\tau_{r+1,K}=\tau_{1,G_rK}\tau_{r,K}$. Starting at $r=1$, substitution of the $r$-factor expression for $\tau_r$ gives the $(r+1)$-factor expression, with the canonical pullback-composition maps. Hence the degree-$r$ finite-field transport used in Step 4 is precisely the $r$-fold one-step transport specified in [def-trf-frobenius-operators].

For the scheme coefficient maps, multiplicativity in [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison] reads $\kappa_{m+n,K}=G_m(\kappa_{n,K})\kappa_{m,P_nK}$, with the specified composition identifications. The formula $u_r=\varphi_r\kappa_{r,K}$ of [def-trf-iterated-weil-map], naturality of $\kappa_m$ at $u_n:P_nK\to K$, and the Weil cocycle give
$$\begin{aligned}
u_mP_m(u_n)&=\varphi_m\kappa_{m,K}P_m(u_n)
=\varphi_mG_m(u_n)\kappa_{m,P_nK}\\
&=\varphi_mG_m(\varphi_n)G_m(\kappa_{n,K})\kappa_{m,P_nK}
=\varphi_{m+n}\kappa_{m+n,K}=u_{m+n}.
\end{aligned}$$
Together with the operator identity already proved, this gives the asserted compatibility on the scheme-Frobenius side as well.

split_report.summary: Rebuilt the earlier split without new nodes. Existing finite-morphism permanence proves properness of iterates by induction. Completed the missing compact-support normalization using a compactification, the absolute-Frobenius comparison on constant sections, and the explicit semilinear exchange/point-transport formulas. Preserved both operator clauses and proved naturality and cocycle identities. Removed the earlier new finite/proper node and the erroneous realization of the entire unit by this proposition. The canonical factorization/trivialization normalization of kappa is written in the statement; otherwise a scalar rescaling gives a counterexample. Returned-delivery repair: rebased the retained split on the current DAG. The reviewed scheme-Frobenius definition now separates its finiteness/radiciality claim into lem-trf-scheme-frobenius-finite-radicial. Step 1 now directly cites that existing statement for finiteness, retains the explicit proper-iterate induction, and has refreshed verbatim citation evidence. All other retained citation excerpts were checked against current statements; no new node or Mathlib search was needed. Independent second reading revalidated all 49 citations and expanded the naturality induction, the finite-field transport induction, and the scheme coefficient-map cocycle into explicit equations.
